# Spatial ggplot visualization

## plotLengthQc

Plot length histograms of V, J, and junction regions.

`plotLengthQc` plots one histogram each for the V length, the J length, and the junction length of the receptors. Used to choose length thresholds for [`filterAirr()`](filterAirr.md).

```r
plotLengthQc(airr_df, bin_width = 5, title = NULL)
```

Arguments:

- `airr_df`: AIRR-style receptor table, or a SIRUP object. The table needs the columns `v_sequence_start`, `v_sequence_end`, `j_sequence_start`, `j_sequence_end`, and `junction_length`.
- `bin_width`: Width of the histogram bins (default 5).
- `title`: Plot title.

Value: A ggplot object with one panel for each length.

## plotReceptors

Plot receptor groups on a tissue image.

`plotReceptors` plots the spots that hold receptors. It colors the spots by receptor group, or by a continuous value.

```r
plotReceptors(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  group_val = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  overlap = "average",
  value = NULL,
  value_colors = c("#FFFFFF", "#000080"),
  value_limits = c(0, NA),
  value_combine = c("mean", "median", "mode", "max", "min", "sum"),
  receptor_size = 1,
  receptor_alpha = 1,
  title = NULL,
  order_points = TRUE,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  receptor_legend_title = NULL,
  show_receptor_legend = TRUE,
  polygons = FALSE,
  polygon_x = "x",
  polygon_y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  polygon_fill = "#0072B2",
  polygon_color = "#0072B2",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  polygon_label = FALSE,
  polygon_label_by = NULL,
  polygon_label_size = 3,
  polygon_label_color = "black",
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object, or a SIRUP object with spatial data and receptors.
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table with a spatial ID column and a group column. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.
- `group`: Name of the `receptors` column that selects and colors the receptor groups, for example `"clone_id"`.
- `group_val`: Values of `group` to plot. If `NULL`, the function uses all non-missing values.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the Seurat spot names. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored field of a SIRUP object, or uses the first standard spatial ID column that it finds.
- `colors`: Colors of the receptor groups. Named colors match the group values. Unnamed colors follow the order of the values.
- `overlap`: Color of a spot that holds more than one receptor group. The function draws such a spot once, as a combined group with the member names joined by `" + "`. With `"average"` (default), the spot gets the mean color of its members. With one color, all combined spots get that color.
- `value`: Color each spot on a continuous gradient and not by group. Give the name of a numeric `receptors` column, or `"count"` for the number of receptors in the spot. You can omit `group` in this mode. If you give it (with `group_val`), the function uses only the matching receptors.
- `value_colors`: Colors of the `value` gradient (default white to navy). Two colors give a low-to-high gradient. More colors give a gradient with several stops, so you can give a palette such as `viridisLite::viridis(9)`.
- `value_limits`: Limits of the `value` scale (default `c(0, NA)`, which starts the scale at zero).
- `value_combine`: How to combine `value` if a spot holds more than one receptor: `"mean"` (default), `"median"`, `"mode"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, or `"sum"`. The function ignores it if `value = "count"`.
- `receptor_size`: Size of the receptor points (default 1).
- `receptor_alpha`: Opacity of the receptor points (default 1).
- `title`: Plot title.
- `order_points`: Draw the early receptor groups first, so that the later groups show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.
- `receptor_legend_title`: Title of the receptor legend. If `NULL`, the function uses `group`.
- `show_receptor_legend`: Show the receptor legend (default `TRUE`)?
- `polygons`: Draw polygons under the points on each spatial panel. With `FALSE` (default), the function draws no polygons. With `TRUE`, it uses the polygons stored in the SIRUP object. You can also give a data frame of polygon vertices, or the path of a CSV file of polygon vertices. A vertex table needs the columns set by `polygon_x` and `polygon_y`. It needs the column set by `polygon_id` if it holds more than one polygon.
- `polygon_x`: Name of the x-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"x"`).
- `polygon_y`: Name of the y-coordinate column in the polygon table (default `"y"`).
- `polygon_id`: Name of the column that separates the polygons in the polygon table (default `"polygon"`). If the column does not exist, the function uses a `polygon` or `polygon_id` column. If neither exists, all rows form one polygon.
- `polygon_val`: IDs of the polygons to draw. If `NULL`, the function draws all polygons.
- `polygon_alpha`: Opacity of the polygon fill (default 0.2).
- `polygon_fill`: Fill color of the polygons (default `"#0072B2"`).
- `polygon_color`: Color of the polygon outlines (default `"#0072B2"`).
- `polygon_linewidth`: Width of the polygon outlines (default 0.6).
- `polygon_label`: Write a label at the center of each polygon (default `FALSE`)?
- `polygon_label_by`: Name of the column that holds the labels. If `NULL`, the function uses the polygon ID.
- `polygon_label_size`: Text size of the polygon labels (default 3).
- `polygon_label_color`: Text color of the polygon labels (default `"black"`).
- `combine`: Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## plotReceptorsExpression

Plot receptor groups over gene expression.

`plotReceptorsExpression` plots one feature together with one or more groups of receptors on a tissue image. For example, it shows the BCR-positive and TCR-positive spots on one expression map.

```r
plotReceptorsExpression(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  group_val = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  feature = NULL,
  gene = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  overlap = "average",
  value = NULL,
  value_colors = c("#FFFFFF", "#000080"),
  value_limits = c(0, NA),
  value_combine = c("mean", "median", "mode", "max", "min", "sum"),
  receptor_size = 1,
  receptor_stroke = 0.7,
  receptor_alpha = 1,
  feature_colors = c("#939393", "#FFFF00"),
  feature_size = 1,
  feature_alpha = 1,
  zero_tol = 0,
  title = NULL,
  order_points = TRUE,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  receptor_legend_title = NULL,
  show_receptor_legend = TRUE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object, or a SIRUP object with spatial data and receptors.
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table with a spatial ID column and a group column. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.
- `group`: Name of the `receptors` column that defines the receptor groups, for example `"receptor_type"` with the values `"BCR"` and `"TCR"`. You can omit it if you give `value`. If you give both, `group` and `group_val` only select the receptors to draw.
- `group_val`: Group values to plot, in the order of the plot. If `NULL`, the function uses all non-missing values of `group`.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the Seurat spot names. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored field of a SIRUP object, or looks for a standard spatial ID column.
- `feature`: Feature to plot under the spots with receptors.
- `gene`: Alias for `feature`.
- `colors`: Colors of the receptor groups. Named colors match the group values. Unnamed colors follow the order of the values.
- `overlap`: Color of a spot that holds more than one receptor group. The function draws such a spot once, as a combined group with the member names joined by `" + "`. With `"average"` (default), the spot gets the mean color of its members. With one color, all combined spots get that color.
- `value`: Color the receptor spots on a continuous gradient and not by group. Give the name of a numeric `receptors` column, or `"count"` for the number of receptors in the spot.
- `value_colors`: Colors of the `value` gradient (default white to navy). Two colors give a low-to-high gradient. More colors give a gradient with several stops.
- `value_limits`: Limits of the `value` scale (default `c(0, NA)`).
- `value_combine`: How to combine `value` if a spot holds more than one receptor: `"mean"` (default), `"median"`, `"mode"`, `"max"`, `"min"`, or `"sum"`. The function ignores it if `value = "count"`.
- `receptor_size`: Size of the receptor circles (default 1).
- `receptor_stroke`: Line width of the receptor circles (default 0.7).
- `receptor_alpha`: Opacity of the receptor circles (default 1).
- `feature_colors`: Colors that make the expression scale (default `c("#939393", "#FFFF00")`).
- `feature_size`: Size of the expression points (default 1).
- `feature_alpha`: Opacity of the expression points (default 1).
- `zero_tol`: Values at or below this threshold count as zero (default 0).
- `title`: Plot title.
- `order_points`: Draw the low expression values first, so that the high values show on top (default `TRUE`)? The function draws the receptor groups in the order of `group_val`.
- `assay`: Assay to use.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use (default `"counts"`).
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes?
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.
- `receptor_legend_title`: Title of the receptor legend. If `NULL`, the function uses `group`.
- `show_receptor_legend`: Show the receptor legend (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine`: Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## plotSpatialCloneColorTips

Plot the tip colors of one clone on a tissue image.

`plotSpatialCloneColorTips` plots the spots of one clone. Each spot gets the color of its tip. The function calls [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md).

```r
plotSpatialCloneColorTips(
  colored_clones,
  clone_val,
  tissue_positions = NULL,
  clone = "clone_id",
  spatial_id = "spatial_id_8um",
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  ...
)
```

Arguments:

- `colored_clones`: Result of [`assignTipColors()`](assignTipColors.md), or a SIRUP object whose receptor table has the tip colors.
- `clone_val`: ID of the clone to plot.
- `tissue_positions`: Seurat object or SIRUP object. Omit it if `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object.
- `clone`: Name of the column that holds the clone IDs (default `"clone_id"`). If `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object and you omit this argument, the function uses the stored clone field.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the column in `colored_clones` that holds the spatial IDs (default `"spatial_id_8um"`). If `colored_clones` is a SIRUP object and you omit this argument, the function uses the stored spatial ID field.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `...`: Other arguments for [`plotSpatialColorTips()`](plotSpatialColorTips.md).

Value: A ggplot object.

## plotSpatialCloneTreePairs

Plot each clone tree next to its tissue map.

`plotSpatialCloneTreePairs` makes two plots for each clone: the lineage tree, and a tissue map of the tips. Each tip has one color in both plots, so you can find a tip of the tree on the tissue.

```r
plotSpatialCloneTreePairs(
  trees,
  object,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone_val = NULL,
  id = "sequence_id",
  sequence_id = id,
  clone = "clone_id",
  color_by = "identity",
  palette = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  zoom = FALSE,
  tipsize = NULL,
  scale = 0.01,
  layout = "rectangular",
  title = TRUE,
  shape_by = ".sirup_spatial_status",
  shape_values = c(spatial = 21, not_spatial = 22),
  tree_layout = NULL,
  tree_tip_size = NULL,
  tree_linewidth = 0.5,
  tip_stroke = 0.3,
  treescale_fontsize = 3.88,
  treescale = NULL,
  treescale_position = c("bottomleft", "topleft", "midleft"),
  spatial_tip_size = 1.6,
  spatial_tip_alpha = 1,
  order_points = FALSE,
  show_spatial_legend = FALSE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  polygons = FALSE,
  polygon_x = "x",
  polygon_y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon_alpha = 0.2,
  polygon_fill = "#0072B2",
  polygon_color = "#0072B2",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  polygon_label = FALSE,
  polygon_label_by = NULL,
  polygon_label_size = 3,
  polygon_label_color = "black",
  nproc = 1L,
  ...
)
```

Value: A named list with one element for each clone. Each element is a list with the items `tree` and `spatial_clone` (the two plots), and `legend` and `legend_rel_height` (for the optional legend).

## sirupSampleFromImage

Get the sample name from an image label.

`sirupSampleFromImage` returns the sample name in an image label.

```r
sirupSampleFromImage(image)
```

Arguments:

- `image`: Character vector of image labels.

Value: A character vector of sample names, with `NA` for each label that has no sample part.

## spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF

Save the tree and map pairs to a PDF file.

`spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF` writes one page for each clone to a PDF file. Each page shows the tree and the tissue map of the clone side by side.

```r
spatialCloneTreePairsToPDF(
  pairs,
  path,
  width = 12,
  height = 6,
  rel_widths = c(1.2, 1),
  nproc = 1L
)
```

Arguments:

- `pairs`: Result of [`plotSpatialCloneTreePairs()`](plotSpatialCloneTreePairs.md).
- `path`: Path of the PDF file.
- `width`: Width of a page, in inches (default 12).
- `height`: Height of a page, in inches (default 6).
- `rel_widths`: Relative widths of the tree panel and the map panel (default `c(1.2, 1)`).
- `nproc`: Number of processes for the pages (default 1). The function needs the `qpdf` package to join the pages that it makes in parallel. If `qpdf` is not installed, it makes the pages one after the other.

Value: `path`, invisibly.

## spatialDiscretePlot

Plot a metadata column on a tissue image.

`spatialDiscretePlot` colors each spot by the value of a metadata column. It leaves out the spots that have the \"zero_value\" value.

```r
spatialDiscretePlot(
  object,
  meta_col,
  zero_value = 0,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  point_size = 1.6,
  point_alpha = 1,
  order_points = TRUE,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `meta_col`: Name of the metadata column to plot.
- `zero_value`: Value that means \"not present\" (default 0). The function does not draw these spots.
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `cols`: Named vector of colors, one for each value.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots. The default is 1.6.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `order_points`: Draw the low numeric values, or the early factor levels, first, so that the high or late values show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.
- `combine`: Combine the panels with patchwork, if possible (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot object, a patchwork object, or a list of plots. The function returns `NULL` if all spots have the blank value.

## spatialExpressionBlendPlot

Blend the expression of two features on a tissue image.

`spatialExpressionBlendPlot` colors each spot by the expression of two features at once. By default, it leaves out the spots where both features are zero.

```r
spatialExpressionBlendPlot(
  object,
  features,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  feature_1_alt_name = NULL,
  feature_2_alt_name = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  only_blended = FALSE,
  bottom_left = "#FFFFFF",
  bottom_right = "#0000FF",
  top_left = "#FFFF00",
  top_right = "#00FF00",
  zero_tol = 0,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  point_size = 0.6,
  point_alpha = 1,
  order_points = TRUE,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `features`: Names of two features.
- `combine`: Combine the panels and the legend with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.
- `feature_1_alt_name`: Label of the first feature in the blend legend. If `NULL`, the function uses the feature name.
- `feature_2_alt_name`: Label of the second feature in the blend legend. If `NULL`, the function uses the feature name.
- `assay`: Assay to use.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use (default `"counts"`).
- `only_blended`: Return only the blended panel and the legend (default `FALSE`)?
- `bottom_left`: Color of the bottom-left corner of the blend grid (low in both features). The default is `"#FFFFFF"`.
- `bottom_right`: Color of the bottom-right corner of the blend grid (high in the first feature). The default is `"#0000FF"`.
- `top_left`: Color of the top-left corner of the blend grid (high in the second feature). The default is `"#FFFF00"`.
- `top_right`: Color of the top-right corner of the blend grid (high in both features). The default is `"#00FF00"`.
- `zero_tol`: Values at or below this threshold count as zero (default 0). Set to -Inf to plot all spots.
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots. The default is 0.6.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `order_points`: Draw the spots with low blended expression first, so that the spots with high expression show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.

Value: A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## spatialExpressionMultiPlot

Plot several features as ordered color layers.

`spatialExpressionMultiPlot` draws each feature in its own color on one tissue image. The features are layers. A feature that the function draws later shows on top.

```r
spatialExpressionMultiPlot(
  object,
  features,
  feat_order = NULL,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  colors = NULL,
  breadth_metric = c("n_expressing"),
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  point_size = 0.6,
  point_alpha = 1,
  order_points = TRUE,
  zero_tol = 0,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `features`: Names of the features to plot.
- `feat_order`: Order of the layers. Put broad features (low priority) first and rare features (high priority) last. If `NULL`, the function orders the features with `breadth_metric`.
- `combine`: Combine the spatial panels and the legends with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.
- `assay`: Assay to use.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use (default `"counts"`).
- `colors`: Colors, one for each feature.
- `breadth_metric`: Measure that sets the default order of the features (default `"n_expressing"`, the number of spots that express the feature).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots. The default is 0.6.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `order_points`: Draw the low-priority features first, so that the high-priority features show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `zero_tol`: Values at or below this threshold count as zero (default 0). Set to -Inf to plot all spots.
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.

Value: A ggplot object or a patchwork object. If `combine = FALSE`, a list.

## spatialExpressionPlot

Plot gene expression on a tissue image.

`spatialExpressionPlot` plots the expression of one or more features. By default, it draws only the spots with expression above zero.

```r
spatialExpressionPlot(
  object,
  features,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  feature_colors = NULL,
  feature_color_palette = "viridis",
  zero_tol = 0,
  point_size = 0.6,
  point_alpha = 1,
  order_points = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `features`: Names of the features to plot.
- `assay`: Assay to use.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use (default `"counts"`).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `feature_colors`: Colors for the continuous expression scale, from the low value to the high value. If you give them, they replace `feature_color_palette`.
- `feature_color_palette`: Color palette for the expression scale, if `feature_colors` is `NULL`: `"viridis"` (default), `"inferno"`, `"plasma"`, `"cividis"`, `"rocket"`, or `"mako"`.
- `zero_tol`: Values at or below this threshold count as zero (default 0). Set to -Inf to plot all spots.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots. The default is 0.6.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `order_points`: Draw the low values first, so that the high values show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `title`: Plot title. For one panel, it replaces the feature name. For several panels that the function combines, it is the title of the whole patchwork, and each panel keeps its feature name.
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the plot shows the full tissue area that the spatial coordinates cover.
- `combine`: Combine the panels into one figure with patchwork, if there are several images or features (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot object, a patchwork object, or a list of plots. The function returns `NULL` if all spots have zero expression.
